Every 'old' anchor in this file was verified by exact string count to occur EXACTLY ONCE in its target file at 98db206 (script-verified). Short SHAs only; no 40-character SHA anywhere; no AI attribution.

OWNER DECISION applied by rev 28: decide() REJECTS PROXIES using util.types.isProxy. isProxy is captured ONCE at module initialization (const { types } = require('node:util'); const isProxy = types.isProxy) and is never read through an argument, a property of page-controlled state or any mutable input. The proxy check runs BEFORE property enumeration, prototype inspection, descriptor access, snapshotting, cloning and freezing, at EVERY accepted container boundary: perRealm, requiredIds, every realm record, and every own value of a record that is not a primitive. Every proxy case returns armed:false, exit 18, shared_worker_block_unverified and NEVER throws and NEVER arms. isProxy detects Proxy objects, including revoked ones, without triggering any trap.

PROXY-27 IS SUPERSEDED IN PLACE AND WITHDRAWN AS A RESIDUAL. No PROXY-27 exception is created or accepted. What honestly remains is narrower and stated: (a) the rule is Node-only (util.types has no browser equivalent, so the decision function is Node-side by contract); (b) an intrinsic captured at module initialization cannot protect against an already-compromised Node process that patched node:util before this module loaded; (c) a NON-Proxy host or exotic object with malicious getters is not covered by isProxy and is handled by the own-data-property, key-order, prototype, snapshot-stability and enumeration checks.

The claim 'pure JavaScript function' is WITHDRAWN EVERYWHERE and replaced by 'deterministic Node-side decision function using a captured standard-library intrinsic'. decide() still performs no I/O, no clock read, no network, no filesystem and no environment read, is synchronous, total and deterministic on Node 22.19.0 and 24.21.0; it is no longer claimed to be implementable in pure ECMAScript.

The explicit 'disagreement' branch of the rev 27 decide() is DELETED as dead code (it was unreachable: clean absence forces typeofSharedWorker==='undefined' for every realm, and any differing non-clean-absence realm is already refused at precedence step 1). FC6 and IC3-d are redefined as reachable rows exercised through the field-validation path, with the exact expected detail realm-not-affirmatively-validated:<id>. The detail string 'disagreement' is WITHDRAWN from the vocabulary and no code may emit it.

ACCESSOR-BEFORE-KEY-ORDER is now canonical: inspectRecordShape runs the own-descriptor/accessor check BEFORE the canonical-key-order check, so a getter or setter on a required key refuses with record-accessor-property (not record-key-order). Sweep C3/C4 expected detail is record-accessor-property.

TEST SEAM (internal module exports only, no public surface, no product-reachable hook): decide(perRealm, requiredIds) is composed of snapshotAndValidate(perRealm, requiredIds) -> {ok:false, result} | {ok:true, snapshot} where snapshot is a frozen array of frozen validated snapshots, and decideFromSnapshot(snapshot) -> verdict. Both are exported for tests so a test can mutate the caller's original objects between validation and decision, including replacing a field with a Proxy or an accessor, and assert the decision is unchanged or a refusal. Product callers use decide() only; no hook, flag, environment variable or configuration key is added (OWNER-25).

IC5 'extra id' is split into two exact sub-cases: IC5-3a a requiredIds-level extra id (22-entry requiredIds) => required-id-set-malformed, and IC5-3b a perRealm-level extra record (22 records, the 22nd a schema-valid record whose id repeats or is out of the required set) => realm-duplicate:<id> or realm-unknown-or-extra:<id>.

FC1 and IC4 are now INDEPENDENTLY EXECUTABLE rows with their own procedure, inputs, expected result and recorded evidence (rev 28 sections J.5 and J.6). F13 and F14 require explicit popup creation by the harness (rev 28 section J.7): the CONF-02 'not-created' outcome is recorded as REALM NOT MEASURED, never as a pass.

Table W6-T is reprinted in full in rev 28 section C and the AUTHORITATIVE ROW COUNT BECOMES 44 ROWS: 21 required decision realms (F1..F21) + 1 informational realm (F22) + 12 decision-function/mechanism cases (FC1..FC12) + 9 control fixtures (IC1..IC9) + 1 carried worker-WebSocket case (FW-1). Added by rev 28: FC12 (proxy rejection at every accepted container boundary, before any enumeration or descriptor access) and IC9 (the seven-case proxy battery: transparent pass-through, trapping, revoked, perRealm-array proxy, requiredIds proxy, nested-value proxy, post-validation substituted proxy). Every live '42 rows' total is superseded by 44.

Sweep counts are derived from the schema constants: |CANONICAL_REQUIRED_REALM_IDS|=21, |REQUIRED_KEYS|=11, |MUTATIONS|=5, |VALID_NEGATIVES|=6, |STRUCTURAL|=13+7=20. Sweep A 21*11*5=1155, Sweep B 21*6=126, Sweep C 20 => 1301 refusals plus EXACTLY ONE authorised armed:true (the B27 positive control) across 1302 decide() invocations. Zero unexpected armed:true is a gate condition, not a warning.

appendText.text: REV 28 (CONF-02, proxy rejection and the withdrawal of the pure-JavaScript claim): decide() is a DETERMINISTIC NODE-SIDE DECISION FUNCTION USING A CAPTURED STANDARD-LIBRARY INTRINSIC, not a pure JavaScript function. It captures isProxy ONCE at module initialization from node:util (require('node:util').types.isProxy) and never reads it through an argument, a mutable input or any page-controlled state. BEFORE any property enumeration, prototype inspection, descriptor access, snapshot, clone or freeze, decide() REJECTS A PROXY AT EVERY ACCEPTED CONTAINER BOUNDARY: perRealm (detail input-proxy:perRealm), requiredIds (input-proxy:requiredIds), every realm record (record-proxy:index-N) and every non-primitive own value of a record (record-value-proxy:KEY:index-N); a proxy substituted after validation is refused or ignored by the frozen snapshot (snapshot-proxy:index-N). Every proxy case yields armed:false, exit 18, shared_worker_block_unverified, never an uncaught exception and never armed; transparent pass-through, trapping, revoked, array-level, requiredIds-level, nested-value and post-validation proxies are all covered, and isProxy detects a Proxy, including a revoked one, without triggering a trap. The rev 27 PROXY-27 residual is WITHDRAWN and superseded by this rule; no exception exists. What remains, stated honestly: the rule is Node-only, an intrinsic captured at initialization cannot protect against an already-compromised process that patched node:util earlier, and a NON-Proxy exotic object with malicious accessors is covered instead by the own-data-property, prototype, key-order, enumeration and snapshot-stability checks. ORDER OF CHECKS IS NORMATIVE: proxy rejection, then plain-object and prototype, then symbol keys, then own-descriptor/accessor (a getter or setter refuses with record-accessor-property), then canonical key order (record-key-order), then snapshot, then types and enumerations, then freeze, then decide. The unreachable 'disagreement' branch and the detail string disagreement are DELETED; realm disagreement is refused through the field-validation path with detail realm-not-affirmatively-validated:ID. decide() is composed of the internal, test-only exports snapshotAndValidate(perRealm, requiredIds) and decideFromSnapshot(snapshot) so post-validation mutation immunity is directly testable; no public surface, flag, environment variable, configuration key or product-reachable hook is added (OWNER-25).

SUPERSEDED AND WITHDRAWN BY REV 28 (ARCH-28, owner decision after CONF-02). NO PROXY-27 EXCEPTION IS CREATED OR ACCEPTED. CONF-02 executed the rev 27 reference decide() and measured the predicted outcome: a pass-through Proxy over an otherwise-valid all-absent base ARMED (armed:true, exit 0), which the owner's rule forbids. Rev 28 replaces the residual with a RULE: decide() captures isProxy once at module initialization from node:util and rejects a Proxy at every accepted container boundary (perRealm, requiredIds, every realm record, every non-primitive own value) BEFORE any enumeration, prototype inspection, descriptor access, snapshot, clone or freeze, so transparent, trapping, revoked, array-level, requiredIds-level, nested-value and post-validation proxies all yield armed:false, exit 18, shared_worker_block_unverified without an uncaught exception. util.types.isProxy identifies a Proxy, including a revoked Proxy, without triggering any trap. The statement 'pure JavaScript cannot distinguish a Proxy...' is withdrawn as a residual because the decision function is no longer claimed to be pure JavaScript: it is a deterministic Node-side decision function using a captured standard-library intrinsic. What honestly remains is narrower and is NOT an arming exception: (a) Node-only dependence - util.types has no browser equivalent, so the decision function is Node-side by contract; (b) an intrinsic captured at module initialization cannot protect against an already-compromised Node process that patched node:util before this module loaded - that is a process-integrity assumption, recorded, not a detection claim; (c) a NON-Proxy host or exotic object with malicious getters is outside isProxy's scope and is covered by the own-data-property, prototype, symbol-key, key-order, enumeration and two-read snapshot-stability checks. Verification is owed to CONF-03 rows FC12 and IC9 (seven proxy cases, each >=3 repetitions per Node version); until CONF-03 executes them this item is CLOSED AS A DESIGN DECISION and OPEN AS A MEASUREMENT OBLIGATION.
